title: Grading 46 futures combo alerts at 12/24/36h: 74 clean checkpoints, 62 stale, and one negative finding I trust.
author: BearsTerritory
selftext:
\*\*TL;DR:\*\* 46 combo alerts, Oct 7-28, graded at 12/24/36h with stale checkpoints excluded. 74 graded checkpoints out of 136 settled. 36h is direction only (13-9, 59%). The only cell worth pointing at is negative: EXPANSION down 5-16, 24%. Exhaustion reads are coin flips on the clean subset. This is a pilot with a working grading harness, not evidence of an edge.  
  
I've been logging option-chain snapshots across nine CME futures products — manual macro log (ZN, DX, VXM, CL, NQ) since late June, IV, 25-delta skew and ATM gamma since early October, options with DTE between 3 and 30 days only. As of this morning: 21,039 observations. This post is about how the alert layer gets graded, not about the app.  
  
\*\*How a combo gets graded\*\*  
  
A combo fires when several structure conditions line up at once. The alert-time ATM price is frozen as base, and it's graded at +12h, +24h, +36h. At each checkpoint I take the observation nearest the mark inside a ±2h window.  
  
Quality first, before W/L counts:  
  
\- verified: ≤15 min off the mark  
\- delayed: 15-120 min off  
\- stale: >120 min off, excluded from W/L. The first print of the next session is stored as evidence, but never counted.  
  
Of 136 settled checkpoints (46 alerts × 3 marks, two still pending): 59 verified, 15 delayed, 62 stale. Roughly a third is clean. I'd rather publish that split than quietly count a print from four hours late.  
  
\*\*What the sample says — 46 alerts, Oct 7-28, stale excluded, 74 graded checkpoints\*\*  
  
12h: 10-17, 37%  
24h: 9-16, 36%  
36h: 13-9, 59%  
  
By read, all windows pooled — 74 checkpoints across 9 read/direction cells:  
  
EXPANSION (down) 5-16, 24%; SELL (short, fired on strength) 12-11, 52%; EXPANSION (up) 4-5, 44%; CAPITULATION (long) 4-3, 57%; BUY (long) 3-3, 50%; BLOWOFF (short) 2-2, 50%; SELL (down variant) 1-1; GAMMA COLLAPSE (down) 0-1; CAPITULATION CONFIRMED (long) 1-0.  
  
These are the app's combo alert types — multi-metric coincidence tests in a rolling window, where SELL and BLOWOFF are short reads and BUY/CAPITULATION are long — not the prediction taxonomy.  
  
\*\*Honest reading, in order of how much I trust it:\*\*  
  
The 12h mark is premature. 37% at 12h against 59% at 36h says the read describes a condition that takes a session or more to resolve. But 13-9 on 22 checkpoints is a p of about 0.26 one-sided — that is not a result, it's a direction of travel. For scale, the 95% Wilson interval on 13/22 is roughly 39% to 77%, which includes a coin flip with room to spare.  
  
Only one cell is worth pointing at. EXPANSION down at 5-16 is p≈0.013 one-sided. Against nine cells that's marginal — Bonferroni-adjusted that's roughly 0.12 — and it's the one thing I'd bet is real.  
  
Checkpoints are not independent draws. Three come from each alert, so 74 graded checkpoints trace back to 46 alerts — 1.6 per alert. EXPANSION down's 21 checkpoints are roughly seven alerts graded three times each. Effective n is the alert count, which means this is a pilot with a working grading harness, not evidence of an edge.  
  
What I'm not claiming: that any of these read types has proven predictive value. Two cells out of nine would look like something on this sample no matter what the underlying process was.  
  
\*\*Regime correlation\*\*  
  
Five regimes, weighted, each of ZN, DX, VXM, CL, NQ normalized 0-100 across its own last 10 manual prints, direction above 55th / below 45th percentile, critical conditions double, wrong critical subtracts, label only above 60%.  
  
This morning: Defensive Risk-Off 89%, Stagflation Pressure 56%, Inflation Shock 50%, Liquidity Relief −44%, Broad Risk-On −63%. Composite Liquidity Pressure 72.3, Inflation Shock 61.4, both elevated.  
  
Equities near the bottom of their range, vol bid, rates bid, dollar firm — defensive. Crude is in the 97th percentile of its own range (the log has it 68 → 101 since late June, and this morning's ATM prints agree within 0.3 handles), and Defensive expects crude down, so the label carries that one miss. Really a defensive tape with an inflationary tail. Whether that CL series is the right contract month is an open check on the ingest side — the prints are internally consistent, I'm not claiming them as a verified market price here.  
  
The correlation that changed my behavior: in a Defensive Risk-Off regime you'd reach for EXPANSION down — fade the rallies. It's the worst cell in the sample at 24%, 5-16, and the one number I'd defend. A naive risk-off mapping loses on this data. What that does not license is the inverse claim that the exhaustion reads win — on the clean subset they're coin flips, and I say that as someone who wanted them to be the answer.  
  
\*\*Testing at zero risk\*\*  
  
Every read is a claim with a timestamp and a price, so it's falsifiable without a position. Paper-entry at the frozen base, grade at 12/24/36, no sizing, no stop, no slippage. The macro side is a 48-hour prediction: +5 for the regime label, ±1 for each of seven directional calls, max 8, public whether it flatters me or not.  
  
\*\*Caveats, plainly\*\*  
  
46 alerts is small. 46% stale means the clean subset is far smaller than the headline. Checkpoints cluster within alerts, so effective n is \~46. Regime weights are hand-set, not fitted. The macro log is human-typed, and there's one keystroke error in there I preserved rather than deleted, flagged as excluded.  
  
Poke holes in the grading logic if you can — I'd rather find the flaw here than from a bad week.
